PSA: Check Your Happy Dragon Orders – Hidden Charges and Mispriced Items

I’ve been a loyal customer of Happy Dragon for several years now, frequently placing orders over $30+. Recently, I decided to question an overcharge I noticed—because this has been happening to me every time I’ve placed an order by phone. My total from the Happy Dragon Restaurant pamphlet came out to be $34.25, but I was charged $35.25. When I asked about the extra $1, I was told by the rude lady it was a “delivery fee.”

I’ve been using their most recent July 2025 menu pamphlet, which replaced the older version a few months ago. Nowhere on this updated menu is a $1 delivery fee mentioned—only a $15 minimum for delivery is clearly listed. After looking further into the charges, I discovered that they automatically include a can of soda with every order—even when I didn’t ask for one—and quietly add a $1 charge for it.

The pamphlet also makes no mention of a free soda with a minimum order, further confirming that the soda is not complimentary but is instead being charged to the customer without consent.

When my food was delivered, I asked the friendly delivery driver if there was a $1 delivery charge or soda fee. He seemed confused, said he wasn’t aware of such a charge, and advised me to ask the restaurant directly. That raised further concerns—even the delivery staff aren’t aware of what customers are being billed for.

There was also a separate instances where I ordered only Chicken with Broccoli and white rice which is priced at $11.50 under the “Chicken” section of the menu pamphlet or only Beef with Broccoli and white rice which is priced at $11.75 under the “Beef” section of the menu pamphlet. Instead, I was charged for both orders under the “Combination Platters” section priced at $13.50 each, which includes pork fried rice and an egg roll—neither of which were included in my order upon delivery. This caused me to be overcharged for an incomplete combo meal I never ordered to begin with, and it’s happened more than once.

While these may seem like small charges, they’re being added without my knowledge or approval—and this has happened every time I’ve placed a phone order over several months, which suggests a clear, intentional pattern. Formal complaints have been filed with the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) & NYC 311. I hope Happy Dragon Chinese Restaurant takes responsibility and improves transparency in their pricing practices.

This is a PSA for all current and new customers placing phone orders: Always double-check your total and request a breakdown of charges, ensuring it matches what’s on their menu pamphlet (which is included on every delivery order). These unlisted fees and misclassifications are misleading and unfair to all Happy Dragon Chinese Restaurant customers.

I’ve been going to this pizzeria since I moved here 11 years ago, and for most of that time, I genuinely loved it. The old family who owned it provided great service, were friendly, and the pizza was always amazing.

Unfortunately, since the business was sold, my experience has been completely different. From the moment we walked in, the new owner just wasn’t friendly. I smiled and tried to greet him when we first came in, and he barely acknowledged us and just had a straight face. I understand that everyone has their own personality, but as a customer, you expect at least a little friendliness and basic customer service.

I ordered four pizzas, and honestly, they were extremely oily and pretty mediocre, especially considering how expensive they are. I also ended up getting a huge stomach ache afterward, which made the experience even worse.

The part that really bothered me, though, was what happened with the tables. This happened twice during our visit. The first time, I sat in a chair closer to the bathroom because I was waiting for it to become available. I didn’t want to keep walking back and forth from our table, and the restaurant wasn’t even busy. While I was sitting there, he came over and started wiping down the table even though it wasn’t dirty and I was still sitting there.

Then, later, my boyfriend and I were sitting at our actual table talking. We were getting ready to leave, and I was only waiting because I wanted to use the bathroom before we left, but it was still occupied. While we were still sitting there and having a conversation, he came over AGAIN and started wiping down our table while we were right there. The table wasn’t dirty, and we weren’t done yet. After that, we decided to just leave instead of waiting around.

I’ve been coming here for 11 years, so it honestly makes me sad to have such a different experience now. review_text:
An incredible Jesuit University in the Bronx.

First I'd like to address the negative reviews. It is a secure campus so no you can't take a walk on the closed secure campus just because you feel like it. Imagine the arrogance of people to leave a negative review of an incredible historic university just because they were told NO.
Then there are the handful of haters who didn't get their fannys patted whole they were students or others who got rejected.. boo hoo.

Now onto the review. Fordham is an incredible university with a global reach.
My wife is an alum and we are on campus all the time and are very involved with the school.
First the physical campus is amazing. Rose Hill is sprawling and beautiful with a ton of green space and mature trees and plantings.
The buildings are beautiful and the new student center is an amazing space.
The sports facilities are great and if you have the chance you should try to get down there for a game whether it's football, basketball , water polo or even rugby. No matter what sport you go to see, it's always a great time.
The staff and the students are always friendly and welcoming !
After you graduate, the connection doesn't end there. The alumni association is strong and holds events all over the country.
We were in Florida and the Fordham baseball team was playing Florida Atlantic University and Fordham had an alumni tailgate at FAU before the game !
Homecoming weekend is a great time to be on campus. The tent on Edwards Parade is a great time as is the tailgate lot which is packed with Fordham pride.
Homecoming always starts with the Ram Run which I proudly run each year.
Academically, Fordham is stronger than ever ! Besides Rose Hill there is the Lincoln Center campus, the London Campus, the Westchester campus and even a biological field station in Westchester.
Fordham also nurtures a students spiritual needs. The campus ministry is strong and well rounded. The campus church is beautiful and we attend Christmas Eve Mass there each year.
Yes the tuition is expensive but you get what you pay for.  The university just received a  $100 million donation to build a new STEM building and increase the schools offerings I'm the sciences.
The school offers a wide array of undergrad and post grad degrees and the networking of the alums allows for greater job opportunities upon graduation.
Look, no school is perfect but Fordham is a fine example of Jesuit higher education and deserves a look from anyone considering higher education.
Take a look at Fordham and join the Ramily!!!

This is a beautiful place with an exceptional atmosphere and excellent service. The ambiance is truly one of the highlights—everything feels thoughtfully designed, elegant, and inviting, and the overall experience is wonderful.

Some of the dishes we tried were very well executed and absolutely delicious. In particular, the Butternut Squash Soup was incredibly good—probably one of the best dishes we had, and I would highly recommend it. The Tempura Shiitakes were also excellent and definitely among our favorites.

That said, some of the other dishes felt a little too focused on presentation rather than flavor. The main courses are very creative and beautifully presented, but some of them fall slightly short in terms of taste. There is also a tendency to use quite a lot of sugar, including in some of the desserts, which makes them feel overly sweet and somewhat heavy on the palate.

Overall, I think there is a lot of creativity and care in the presentation, but the flavors could be a little more balanced and refined. Still, the atmosphere, service, and overall setting are absolutely wonderful, and the Butternut Squash Soup and Tempura Shiitakes alone are worth trying.
